# promper

> breakdown is the one-shot prompt expander in the promper toolkit for AI coding agents.
> One rough sentence in, a fully engineered, ready-to-run plan out. It runs on Claude Code
> and Codex, is free and Apache-2.0 licensed, and spawns nothing until you say go.

## What breakdown does

Where `/promper` engineers a single prompt, `breakdown` engineers the whole run, in six moves:

1. A batched requirements interview turns your answers into a PRD (or ingest a spec with `--prd`).
2. `promper classify` splits the PRD into domain nodes using fixed trigger tables with zero AI,
   so the same input always produces the same breakdown.
3. With Beads (`bd`) installed, the run is filed as an epic plus one issue per node with
   dependencies wired in (opt-in, non-blocking, `--no-beads` to skip).
4. Each node is routed to a specialist agent and inherits that agent's real persona and toolkit;
   Lean CTX context prescriptions are folded in when present.
5. Each node ships as one engineered Claude-native prompt (role, context, instructions,
   constraints, output format). `--target=costar` emits portable prompts instead.
6. You get a parallel-lane execution plan and nothing spawns. `--run` executes it, deciding
   per node between inline work and a subagent.

## Artifacts

Every run lands on disk in `.promper/<slug>/`:

- `PRD.md` — the written spec
- `graph.json` — nodes and dependencies
- `plan.md` — the parallel-lane plan
- `prompts/` — one engineered prompt per node

## Optional dependencies

- Beads (steveyegge/beads) — git-native, dependency-aware issue tracker for AI agents.
- Lean CTX (yvgude/lean-ctx) — context layer that decides what an agent reads and compresses
  what it sends.

Both are independent open-source projects; breakdown integrates with them but ships without either.

## Singularity

`/promper:singularity <goal>` wraps the same goal contract and graph in a bounded runtime.
It executes ready nodes, collapses their results into compact evidence, evaluates every
acceptance criterion, and adds one focused remediation node when a concrete gap remains.

The first invocation is plan-only unless `--run` is present. Defaults cap a run at four orbits
and twelve total nodes. A run succeeds only when its weighted score reaches the threshold,
every blocking criterion passes, and each pass has a concrete evidence reference. Otherwise
it stops at an event horizon and writes an honest partial result that can be resumed.
